summary: Forestry Commission fire lookout in Berkeley County that the lookout-history site marks as removed; no source found describes the site today.

facts.status_note: The lookout-history site marks the tower as removed.

evidence.supports: Listed under Berkeley County and the South Carolina Forestry Commission
evidence.quote: Berkeley County - South Carolina Forestry Commission

evidence.supports: Commission closed its last forest fire lookout tower on October 1, 1993
evidence.quote: On October 1, the Forestry Commission closed the last of its forest fire lookout towers.

evidence.supports: The tower system had served the state since the 1930s
evidence.quote: The tower system had served the state since the 1930s.

evidence.supports: First towers built in the 1930s, at a time of rising wildfire risk
evidence.quote: The first were built in the 1930s, at a time when deforestation and poor farming practices had increased the risk of wildfires in rural areas of the state

evidence.supports: Statement came from a commission spokesperson
evidence.quote: Michelle Johnson, Forestry Commission spokesperson, said.

evidence.supports: Small cab atop the towers where an operator watched for smoke
evidence.quote: Perched atop the towers was a small cab where a tower operator would periodically climb during dry weather to check for smoke on the horizon.

sources.title: Fire towers stand as a reminder of SC's rural past

notes_for_editor: Only the tower's own listing on the lookout-history site (name, county, agency, removed) and the index page were found. Two searches and the cached pages turned up no Oakley-specific build date, height, staffing, fire or site description. The record's coordinates were not checked. The commission's tower index also lists a separate private Berkeley County tower (Tuxbury Lumber Company), which is a different structure and was not used. Statewide context comes from the commission's wildfire history and a Post and Courier article.
